newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-INJURY RULES EVANS OUT OF SECOND TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-INJURY RULES EVANS OUT OF SECOND TEST.

text.p: Winger Ieuan Evans, the most experienced member of the British Lions squad, has been ruled out of Saturday's second test and possibly the rest of the tour because of injury.
Evans will miss the King's Park test because of of groin injury sustained during the Lions 25-16 win over South Africa in the first test in Cape Town last Saturday.

"Ieuan is not 100 percent fit and he has been ruled out of Saturday's match on medical advice. He might also have to miss out on the rest of the tour but we'll be making a decision about that later today," Lions spokesman Bob Burrows said on Thursday.
John Bentley, top try scorer so far on the tour, is likely to earn his first British Lions test cap as the replacement for Evans.
The strong-running Bentley made another powerful case for his inclusion on Tuesday with a hat-trick of tries against Free State.

Earlier this week, the 30-year-old celebrated his recall to the England squad after a nine-year interlude playing rugby league. He was named in the England squad for the one-off test against Australia in Sydney next month after the end of the Lions tour.
"I've been very pleased with my form on tour and, to be honest, I don't really think I could have done much more to break into the test side for Newlands," Bently said.
"But that was the selectors' decision although it was a great disappointment.

"On Tuesday morning, I remember jokingly suggesting that two tries against Free State -- one in each half -- would give me a chance of breaking into the test side. The hat-trick was a rather pleasant bonus!"
